parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High Risk. Traveller-facing exposures: passport sex-marker restrictions with reported confiscation and stranding; entry refusal for document discrepancies, with a fraud-ground lifetime ineligibility route; federal immigration custody with documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse; corrections policies mandating conversion-type treatment; and counterterrorism framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups. The division adds a school-ground facilities rule binding adult visitors to birth-certificate restrooms, and removed its gender-identity anti-discrimination protection with no state remedy. Mitigators: no national presentation offence, same-sex marriage recognised, and federal litigation that is partly blocked. Violence is undocumented for the division and undercount figures are not used. Federal custody and entry exposures outweigh the protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Cable instructs refusal of cases with document discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex; fraud-ground lifetime ineligibility is possible though not automatic. Passports confiscated or blocked, with reported stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Ineligibility requires all four fraud elements and has limited waivers; the policy is challenged in national courts and not all measures are in effect.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport mismatch triggers entry questioning, which can escalate into fraud allegation and then detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Corrections policy mandates conversion-type treatment; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document or fraud allegation at entry can lead into immigration custody, where the documented harms then apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars facilities congruent with gender identity in government-funded settings. In the division, the school-ground rule covers all persons, including visitors, using birth-certificate-matched restrooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Restroom-trespass arrest is documented in a different unit; no adult restriction outside school grounds is documented for this division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Campus visits by adult visitors fall under the school rule regardless of federal policy; enforcement against adult visitors is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; proposed rules to bar public reimbursement for minors. Division litigation kept adult surgery coverage available.
care_services.protection: Adult surgery coverage was preserved by state court litigation (2019).
care_services.interaction: Records and reimbursement changes affect a minor's care, and a visitor's medical records can reach federal process.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for rapid neutralisation; reward system for identifying leadership. Officials frame gender diversity as a threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states that powers will not target people who simply disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat framing combined with document checks raises the chance of discovery leading to enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in 27 states. A minor travelling with a guardian meets school-ground birth-certificate rules and possible records subpoenas. Conversion-type treatment is lawful for minors in most of the country.
minors_guardians.protection: Guardian consent allows a single-person facility accommodation at schools; a city-level ban on conversion therapy for minors exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor may be placed in a facility by birth certificate, while the guardian faces the same rule on school grounds.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific violence figures; the monitoring analysis reports undercount floors only. One unit's restroom arrest was a trespass prosecution, not a street assault.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute applies nationally; 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes. Federal police prosecuted some bias cases.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to assaults on visitors is not documented in this division.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state remedy for refusal of service, housing or employment on gender identity; 2026 law bars stronger local protections. Federal orders remain partly enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal employment protection exists; 22 states plus the capital district prohibit gender-identity discrimination in other units.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The division's removal of protections means a visitor's remedy depends on federal channels, which are contested.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-one exposure: birth-sex facility and ward rules with failed remedies. This case is lower because it adds federal immigration custody abuse, entry refusal for document discrepancy and threat-framing, but it lacks the 0.35-A's universal public-building exclusion across the whole country.

Similar: birth-sex facility rules, recurring official abuse and failed remedies. This case is similar in severity, with no documented street extortion or raids. Its national custody and entry exposures are comparable.

Lower-tier comparison: 0.15-D has a registry, disclosure at checkpoints and fraud prosecutions with execution-adjacent custody. This case has no registry, no national presentation offence and no documented sweeps, so it is clearly higher.

parsed.synthesis: Traveller-facing exposures are mainly tier one and two: document-mismatch entry refusal with a fraud-ground route, federal custody abuses, and facility rules that bind adult visitors on school grounds. Threat framing raises discovery-to-enforcement chains. Protections (no national presentation offence, national hate-crime statute, marriage recognition, partly enjoined orders) do not offset the documented custody and entry harms. The division's removal of protections without remedy leaves no operative state recourse. Violence is undocumented and not inferred from undercount floors.
